claim_counterparty: EP Carbon / Acorn; Gold Standard; Verra VCS; Henkel (buyer); L'Oréal (buyer); IKEA (buyer)
source_name: Acorn EP Carbon Season 1–3 project documentation; Gold Standard VCU registry; RONGEAD 2019 Shea Value Chain Report
notes: Shea parkland carbon credits are issued against verified CO2 sequestration by shea trees. Physical backing: ~2.7M tCO2e verified in Acorn S1-S3. Abstract issued: 4.2M tCO2e (Acorn alone). Coupling risk: additionality concerns (shea trees were there before the project), permanence risk (climate stress, land clearing), leakage. Coupling estimated at 0.65 reflecting ~35% discount for permanence and additionality uncertainty. Not rehypothecated but same credit may be counted in multiple corporate Scope 3 registries.

claim_counterparty: Fairtrade International; Cooperative network (WAGRIB Burkina Faso; Savannah Fruits Ghana; AON Ghana; ADAF Ghana); cosmetic/food buyers
source_name: RONGEAD 2019 Shea Value Chain Analysis; KPMG 2018 Sector Review; Fairtrade International annual reports; Rainforest Alliance sourcing reports
notes: PRIMARY DECOUPLING. Research consistently shows only 10–30% of Fair Trade certified shea volumes actually receives the farmgate premium. Estimated: ~120,000t certified globally; ~15,000t receives documented premium. Brand buyers report 100% of volume in sustainability disclosures as 'Fair Trade certified'. Collectors receive standard market price for remainder. This is the shea chain's equivalent of gold's unallocated account problem: abstract certification claims vastly exceed verified premium delivery. Not financial rehypothecation — structural certification gap.

claim_counterparty: ECOCERT; Soil Association; USDA NOP; certified processors in Ghana/Burkina Faso/Mali (Savannah Fruits; KARITE PLUS; Olvea)
source_name: ECOCERT Africa certification registry; processor annual reports; Export Promotion Authority Ghana
notes: Organic certification requires physical field inspection and chain-of-custody documentation. Coupling is relatively high (0.78) compared to Fair Trade because third-party auditors conduct real site visits. Gap reflects: some double-counting with Fair Trade certification; minor yield estimation errors; small volumes included without full traceability back to specific farms. Most reliable certification layer in the shea chain.

claim_counterparty: Standard Chartered; Ecobank; Stanbic IBTC; IFC commodity finance programs; PROPARCO
source_name: IFC commodity finance documentation; Standard Chartered trade finance reports; Ghana Export Promotion Authority statistics
notes: Letters of credit are backed by bills of lading and warehouse receipts. High coupling — financial instrument is cancelled by physical delivery. Standard documentary trade finance structure. Minor 0.05 slippage from renegotiated terms, partial shipments, and credit note adjustments. Not rehypothecated.

claim_counterparty: AAK; IOI Loders Croklaan; Fuji Oil; Cargill; Wilmar International
source_name: Commodity trade desk filings; AAK annual report; IOI Group sourcing disclosures; UNCTAD commodity finance review 2022
notes: Larger buyers lock in supply price via bilateral OTC forward contracts. No central clearing or exchange registration. Coupling below 1.0 due to: contract re-negotiation when market moves sharply (common in soft commodity markets), partial delivery acceptance, and some speculative positioning by commodity traders. Volume estimate from UNCTAD and buyer disclosure analysis.

claim_counterparty: L'Oréal (Shea Butter Sourcing Program); Unilever (Sustainable Living Plan); BASF; Evonik; AAK; Johnson & Johnson; Clarins; The Body Shop
source_name: L'Oréal Sustainability Report 2023; Unilever Sustainable Living Plan 2022; BASF Beauty Ingredients sourcing policy; Global Shea Alliance membership disclosures
notes: SECOND MAJOR DECOUPLING POINT. Companies market approximately $1.9B worth of 'sustainable shea' cosmetics and food products annually. Traceability typically extends only to tier-1 aggregator — not to specific cooperatives or collectors. Physical backing is the proportion of volume with verified chain-of-custody documentation back to farm level (estimated $800M, sourced via verified GSA-compliant schemes). Coupling 0.42 reflects the structural gap between brand-level sustainability claims and farm-level verification. Analogous to gold's ETF market but with an authenticity rather than financial coupling problem.

claim_counterparty: Retail brands (LVMH; Estée Lauder; H&M Beauty; Boots; Sephora; Target; Walmart); private label manufacturers
source_name: EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009 enforcement reports; EU Green Claims Directive 2024 impact assessment; Nielsen sustainable consumer survey 2023; Mintel natural cosmetics market data
notes: Consumer-facing 'natural', 'organic', '100% shea butter', 'fair trade certified', 'ethically sourced' labels on retail cosmetics and food products. EU Cosmetics Regulation requires safety dossier but does not mandate supply chain claim verification. Coupling 0.45 reflects: verified organic/FT claims (high coupling ~0.80) are minority; majority of 'natural' and 'sustainable' claims are marketing language with weak regulatory backing. EU Green Claims Directive (2024) expected to force substantiation — significant compliance exposure for brands. Physical backing estimated as products with independently verified sourcing claims.
